newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up after hitting new highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up after hitting new highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Tuesday but off new contract highs for the front months on Southwestern cooling demand and stronger physical power prices, industry sources said.
"Mostly (the strength) came from weather, but cash prices were stronger today," one New York-based futures trader said.

June Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up 73 cents at $23.10 after reaching a new contract high of $23.60 and trade as low as $22.70 per megawatt hour (MWh), while July settled up 52 cents at $25.60 after trade in a range of $25.35-25.85 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished between five and 35 cents higher.

June California Oregon Border (COB) closed up 45 cents at $17.02 after hitting a new contract high of $17.75 and a low of $16.90, while July ended up 43 cents at $18.35 after trading at a new contract high of $18.90 and as low as $18.25 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished between 10 and 40 cents higher.

Western physical power prices were said to be higher, with firm, peak PV power for Wednesday delivery rising to $28.00-29.00 from $23.00-24.00 on Monday for Tuesday delivery, while at COB, next-day prices firmed to $18.00-18.50 from yesterday's $17.00-18.00.
Weather was said to be the prime mover behind the physical power rise, with forecasts of hot weather in the interior sections of the Southwest expected to keep air-conditioning demand high.
Sources expected the strength to continue, at least over the short term.
"We'll likely see one more push (in power futures) to the upside tomorrow morning," the New York trader said.
The NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas contract finished down 3.5 cents at $2.189 per million British thermal units.
Most of the Southwest was forecast to see dry and warmer-than-normal spring temperatures through next week. The California coast was called to see seasonal readings in the high-60s to low-80s.

A warm, dry weather system was expected to stay over the Northwest into next week. Temperatures would run well above normal in the western sections, above normal in the central areas, and near normal in the eastern region.
Also, the Bonneville Power Administration plans to boost transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from 6,250 MW at midnight tonight.
